## What's new in DiskScope 1.1

- **Sunburst view (⌘4).** A third view next to List and Columns: a ring chart of the folder you're in, one ring per folder level, each slice sized by disk usage. Hover a slice for details, click it to drill in, click the center to go up. A "Largest items" legend sits alongside.
- **"Not in scan".** When you scan a whole disk, DiskScope now shows how much of the used space the scan couldn't see, and why: other volumes on the same disk (VM swap, Preboot, Recovery…), Time Machine local snapshots, folders it couldn't read, and system data. Purgeable space is noted. It's in the status bar, and a gray slice in the sunburst.
- **Find Duplicates.** Pick a folder, and optionally a second folder to compare it with. Files are matched by size, then by SHA-256 checksum, and duplicate sets are listed with the biggest savings first. Compare two copies side by side: text, images, video and audio (with Play Both), PDFs, or a Quick Look thumbnail. iCloud and Dropbox placeholders are skipped so nothing gets downloaded, symlinks are never followed, and hard links aren't counted as duplicates.
- **You stay in control of removing duplicates.** Find Duplicates never deletes or moves anything itself. Mark each copy Keep or Remove (or apply a rule: keep the copy in Folder A, in Folder B, the oldest, the newest, or the one with the shortest path; every set always keeps at least one copy). Then **Removal Script…** saves a bash script for you to read and run in Terminal: `bash remove-duplicates.sh` is a dry run, and `bash remove-duplicates.sh --apply` moves the marked files to the Trash. Before each move the script re-checks with `shasum -a 256` that the file and the copy being kept are still identical, and skips anything that changed. The script is saved without execute permission.
- **Export CSV.** Export the folder you're viewing or the whole scan (path, kind, size on disk, apparent size, items, modified), or the duplicate sets (set, SHA-256, size, copies, wasted space, folder, keep/remove, path, modified). Values that a spreadsheet could treat as formulas are neutralised.
- **Ask Claude (optional).** A panel on the right of the browser (toolbar button) where you can ask questions about your scan, like "What's using the most space?" or "What can I safely delete?". It's off until you turn it on and add your own Anthropic API key (create one at https://platform.claude.com/settings/keys; the Settings tab walks you through it) in DiskScope › Settings. The key is stored in the macOS Keychain, and usage is billed to your key. It uses Claude Opus 5.5. When you press Send, DiskScope sends a text summary of the scan to Anthropic's API over HTTPS: names relative to the scan root (your home folder shown as `~`), sizes, dates and the "Not in scan" breakdown. "What gets sent" shows exactly what will be sent first. File contents are never sent, and Claude can only answer: it can't open, move or delete anything.
- **Downloads.** DiskScope is now published here as a DMG, built and tested automatically by GitHub Actions.
- **More accurate startup-disk totals.** Software Update's second mount of the system volume is no longer counted twice when scanning `/`.

DiskScope works offline by default. The only network feature is the optional Ask Claude panel, and it sends nothing until you enable it and press Send. File contents are read only by Find Duplicates (to compute checksums) and its previews, locally, and are never uploaded.
